findings.text: The lane separates classic suspend from suspend to idle at the platform layer. One operations table serves classic states and a different table serves the idle state. Early, late and no-interrupt preparation each consult only the table that matches the requested state, and the resume side mirrors that split with early restore for idle and wake plus finish for classic states. Absent hooks are equivalent to immediate success with no further action.

Two weak architecture hooks bracket the low level suspend window with interrupt masking control. Their in-tree defaults only disable and re-enable local delivery, and an architecture may replace either default without changing callers.

Hibernation load wraps bitmap creation, image retrieval and image activation under a single hotplug exclusion, releasing devices and bitmaps on any failure. Activation itself quiesces consoles and devices before platform preparation, then pauses idle handling and reduces processor count, then moves through interrupt masking and a global suspend mark into system core suspension and processor state capture around high memory handling and the architecture transfer. Success does not return through the normal path, while failure unwinds symmetrically through processor restore, core resume, interrupt and state restoration, processor re-enablement, platform cleanup and device plus console recovery.

Platform specific hibernation callbacks are conditional on both a caller supplied platform mode request and the presence of a hibernation operations table. Without either condition the pre restore step reports success and the cleanup step does nothing.

Image loading advances on a monotonically increasing cursor rather than explicit seeks. An initial stage acquires shared staging, a header stage validates compatibility and creates working sets while starting page protection, a metadata stage decodes original frame identities and prepares safe destinations, and a data stage delivers one page per step with special handling for high memory and protected pages. Entries marked as zero are materialised as cleared pages without consuming stored data, and a flag records whether the current destination aliases the shared staging area. Exhaustion is signalled distinctly from data delivery and from failure.

A stored image is accepted only when version, operating system identity strings for name release version and machine, and total physical memory size all match the running kernel. Any mismatch is reported as a permission problem with a textual reason, and the loader derives copy and metadata counts from header totals only after acceptance.

Metadata words encode an original frame number together with a zero marker. The loader rejects frames that are invalid or outside the expected set, emitting a firmware oriented diagnostic for invalid frames, and otherwise records the frame while separately tracking zero marked frames and their total.

Two global page classification maps are always created and destroyed as a pair. Repeated creation when both already exist succeeds immediately, while the presence of exactly one is treated as a fatal inconsistency. Creation seeds one map from configured no-save address ranges with debug logging, and destruction warns on incomplete state before clearing both globals.

The lane supports builds with and without high memory through paired variants of the same helpers. One build reports no high memory pages and trivial success for restore, buffering and flushing. The other build counts high memory frames in the image, bounds safe high memory reservation by current free high memory, exchanges page contents through a temporary buffer, and flushes a pending high memory page when present.

Resume signature handling reads the designated resume block and compares a short prefix against the expected hibernation marker. On a match the original marker bytes are restored and written back synchronously, while a mismatch is reported as a missing device. Both outcomes then release all previously allocated image swap slots by draining an extent tree range by range and freeing each extent node.

Swap based image retrieval first primes the snapshot loader to obtain a header page, then opens a swap reader and fetches the header. The stored mode flag selects between plain and compressed payload loading for the remaining pages, after which the reader is always finalised. Success and failure produce distinct debug diagnostics.

Two exclusion scopes protect hibernation. Device hotplug is held for the whole load plus activation attempt including error cleanup. Local interrupts are masked across the inner suspend mark, core suspension, processor capture and architecture transfer, and are restored together with the running mark before processors are re-enabled. Architecture defaults provide the masking primitives.

Allocation failure anywhere in staging, bitmap creation, safe page reservation or backup entry allocation aborts the load with an out of memory signal and releases partial image state where required. A failed architecture transfer is attributed to memory pressure and therefore frees image state immediately before processor and core restoration to maximise reclaim.

Suspend timing is measured in kernel ticks converted to milliseconds, logged with a caller label, and warned upon when exceeding a configured suspend duration threshold. Hibernation failures surface through error logs for missing signatures, load errors, device power down refusal and memory map mismatch, with permission and fault signals distinguishing compatibility from corruption cases.

Snapshot progress is represented by a cursor count, a current destination pointer and a flag indicating aliasing of shared staging. Bitmap position is represented by a current frame number. Extent nodes carry inclusive offset bounds, backup entries link an original destination with its safe staging page, and the image header carries total, image and metadata page counts plus version and identity fields used for compatibility.

Globally reachable services in this lane include hibernation activation and its weak processor control, architecture interrupt hooks, suspend timing start and finish, swap signature clearing and swap reclamation plus swap image retrieval, basic bitmap creation and release, snapshot page supply, and high memory restore in both header and source variants. Remaining helpers are file local.
Hibernation resume validation operates on a ten octet signature prefix, comparing the stored prefix and restoring a ten octet original value on success.

Suspend dispatch uses a distinct idle state value versus classic suspend states, hibernation device transitions use separate quiesce and recover message values, the global system state distinguishes suspended from running, and image handling uses separate platform mode and no compress mode flag bits.

Before image preparation the free classification is cleared and then repopulated as a copy of the original frame set, marking those frames unsafe and resetting the unsafe allocation count. Safe page reservation and preallocation are sized from copy plus zero totals minus high memory and unsafe portions, rounded up for chaining structures.

Destination selection prefers direct reuse when the original frame was already reserved as safe and free. Otherwise a backup entry with a freshly reserved safe page is chained for later atomic restoration. High memory frames follow a dedicated high memory path, and running past the expected frame set is reported as a fault.
